reason: The can't-miss list in Q6 is a list of ETIOLOGIES of delirium. Catatonia is a syndrome that co-occurs with delirium, not a cause of it. The vignette's goal-directed behavior (pulling at the IV, trying to leave, swinging at staff) is not catatonic. So the omission is real but low-yield here, and I downgraded it. The underlying point is sound: Wilson et al. found catatonia co-occurring with delirium in critically ill patients, and high-potency D2 blockade can precipitate malignant catatonia. The reviewer's first citation title is garbled; the correct paper is Wilson JE et al., 'Delirium and Catatonia in Critically Ill Patients', Crit Care Med 2017;45:1837-44 (recall). I reworded the correction to frame catatonia as co-occurring or mimicking rather than as a cause.
evidence: Recall: Wilson JE et al., Crit Care Med 2017;45(11):1837-1844; BAP catatonia guideline 2023 (PMID 37039129) on antipsychotic risk in catatonia.
